phases.evidence: Repository metadata, public claims, examples, canonical CLI smoke checks, native execution of the Sotlas-written lexer subset, and an integrated Sotlas-written compiler frontend that rejects malformed input, unsupported aggregate members, invalid break/continue/return context, unresolved local names and direct function calls, mismatched direct-call arity, mismatched arguments with explicit identifier types or homogeneous declared arithmetic operands, known return type mismatches, missing values in typed return statements, and typed functions whose represented sequential/if-else paths can fall through, all with source locations; it also accepts typed functions whose explicit if/else branches both return or whose return is nested in an unsafe block, rejects duplicate top-level declarations, parameters, and same-block locals, and compiles a program with parameters, mutable locals, and a return nested in unsafe to executable C.
phases.boundary: The native frontend is an experimental seven-module parser/emitter subset with limited lexical and structural semantic checks; resolution is limited to functions declared in the same module, imported and foreign symbol resolution, literal/coercion/comparison/aggregate type inference, all-path return proofs for loops or arbitrary CFG, a complete semantic analyzer, and production replacement are not implemented, and it is not a stage1/stage2 fixed-point proof.

phases.evidence: Canonical check pipeline and typed AST semantic cases; undeclared names retain source locations and offer a close-name suggestion only when a visible symbol is a strong match. Quarantine alias analysis joins every possible owner origin across if/else paths, rejects stale reads, permits an unconditional local rebind after invalidation, and remains conservative for loop paths.
phases.boundary: Most semantic cases are checker tests; native execution is limited to explicit fixtures. General path-sensitive alias invalidation remains outside the contract.

phases.evidence: Canonical ownership/SIR placement, symbolic REGION arena/lifetime graph composition, path-sensitive reaching-epoch certificates for acyclic points, activation entries, canonical loop recurrences, and source-level same-binding handover in both if/else arms with a single post-join consumer and a complete-coverage same-typed producer merge certificate, static rejection, method escape checks with path-merged alias origins across branches and loops, legacy native probes, and production C11 execution of the supported region, direct, whisper, ISLAND-to-EXCLUSIVE handover, and repr(C) external-wrapper subsets. Native caller probes check destructor counts and transferred field values. Canonical CLI integration cases also check consuming move calls followed by handover and quarantine through graph validation, SIR placement, and Target IR reporting.
phases.boundary: REGION arena facts are symbolic; disjoint same-typed CFG producer alternatives require complete branch-path coverage. Method alias propagation improves escape checks for represented structured statements, while broad lifetime proofs remain open. Only the tested same-binding handover branch shape is represented in source SIR; arbitrary branch ownership remains fail-closed. Physical arena allocation/reuse, arbitrary CFG, and full runtime ARC remain outside the contract.

phases.evidence: Canonical authority checks, typed SIR facts, and ABI contract validation.
phases.boundary: Reference ABI tests do not imply vendor GPU/NPU execution.

phases.evidence: Canonical state typing and transition validation.
phases.boundary: Only declared state-transition forms are accepted.

phases.evidence: Effect inference and backend rejection contracts.
phases.boundary: Effect checking does not sandbox external side effects.

phases.evidence: Canonical typed plans/SIR; the reference CPU runner interprets pure integer/boolean stages and schedules independent layers with error/cancellation propagation. The executable serial SIR CFG scheduler lowers fixed-width signed add/subtract/multiply returns, checks signed input/result ranges, executes signed stages, and rejects overflow before returning a Flow result. It executes source-derived stage functions with scalar conditional branches, loop-carried phi joins, and backedges after Target IR validation; unreachable-block, unsupported-operation, and unsupported-type cases fail closed. Cooperative cancellation is checked at every block entry; non-terminating execution is bounded by one million block visits. C11 entrypoints execute pure scalar integer, f32/f64, and bool graphs in deterministic dependency order, including graphs with independent stages. C and Sotlas callers can invoke the generated entrypoint through its checked C ABI declaration; a companion ABI returns all stage outputs and checks caller pointers. A native `_cancelable` ABI polls between stages, reports cancellation status/index, and publishes outputs only on success. A native `_dispatch` ABI invokes a caller-supplied scalar executor with the checked topological index, stable stage name, and scalar type names, propagates executor failure status and cancellation, and commits outputs only on success; C integration tests execute success, failure, and cancellation paths. Independent-stage outputs are compared with the reference runner. `flow-run --backend c11` compiles, executes, and reports checked scalar plans, including stage functions with structured branches and early returns.
phases.boundary: The reference interpreter and native backend cover different instruction/type subsets; generated C11 signed overflow is not defined by the language. Signed arithmetic validation applies to the serial SIR interpreter and is not a defined C11 arithmetic contract. C11 uses a serial fallback and does not promise parallel speedup. Source calls require the exact generated symbol and an @system function; there is no dedicated Flow invocation syntax. Direct native stage functions are restricted to proven-pure scalar functions and cannot report stage failures; cancellation is cooperative. `_dispatch` callbacks are caller-supplied and are not proven equivalent to Sotlas stage bodies; only scalar values are supported. Ownership payloads, CFG operations outside the validated scalar subset, and built-in GPU/NPU dispatch remain unsupported.

phases.evidence: Target normalization, feature contracts, and LLVM emission checks.
phases.boundary: This is not a complete platform ABI or a Sotlas machine-code backend.

phases.evidence: Checked DEVICE lifecycle and reference provider failure contracts, plus an optional native OpenCL f32 vector-add dispatched by Sotlas-generated C11 code and verified with a C caller. A tested runtime policy selects CPU, requires OpenCL, or falls back to CPU when the runtime/GPU is unavailable and reports the chosen backend. GPU enumeration and index selection are tested. OpenCL event profiling separates input uploads, kernel execution, and readback. On Linux, a fault-injecting OpenCL provider exercises 12 initialization, dispatch, readback, and profiling failures without a physical GPU and aborts if any acquired handle leaks.
phases.boundary: OpenCL covers one explicit C ABI kernel; enumeration indices are not persistent hardware identifiers. The simulated provider validates host-side cleanup only and does not validate hardware behavior. Flow stages are not lowered to GPU; NPU, vendor-specific memory domains, async APIs, and full host-to-host benchmark reporting remain unavailable.

phases.boundary: Trust labels do not create process isolation or a sandbox.

phases.evidence: Selection among checked eligible Flow alternatives, fallback reports, and explicit provider availability requirements. Non-CPU execution requires a bound provider executor; executor results are checked against the selected stage set and scalar Sotlas types, including integer ranges. Aggregate outputs must carry a matching sotlas_type_name or type_name tag.
phases.boundary: Provider availability and executor bindings are supplied by the caller; there is no built-in Flow-to-GPU lowering or physical-device discovery.

phases.evidence: Canonical SIR facts, validation, and reports.
phases.boundary: SIR body lowering remains a certified subset, not complete lowering for the language.

phases.evidence: Direct LLVM subset emission and native execution, including source-to-SIR lowering of an unsigned counter/accumulator loop with loop-carried phi nodes, object emission, and execution through a C caller; plus C11/LLVM differential checks for unsigned parameter/literal addition, subtraction, multiplication, defined wraparound, signed comparison inputs, and f32 multiplication and f64 addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and all six comparison predicates, including NaN behavior.
phases.boundary: Parity covers only tested forms. The generated loop is one unsigned counter/accumulator pattern; general mutable loop bodies and ownership cleanup in loop CFG remain unsupported. LLVM provides target code generation; Sotlas does not yet own register allocation or a machine backend.

phases.evidence: Deterministic reports for checked contracts, Flow, and SIR, plus fail-closed pre-selection Target IR v1 with preserved ownership/state annotations, checked structured branch/phi values, validation of phi predecessor/type agreement and SSA dominance, CFG live-in/live-out and SSA interference reports with phi edge uses, an inspection-only linear-scan virtual register-allocation preview for single-block scalars, and a target-neutral aligned local-slot layout preview.
phases.boundary: Target IR reports only the supported checked subset; semantic annotations do not execute and tested structured CFG does not imply arbitrary CFG support. Virtual register assignments and abstract frame layouts are not consumed by code generation; target register classes, coalescing, spill/reload emission, platform ABI layout, and machine-code emission remain open.
